title_idea: EU imposes provisional tariff-rate quota safeguard measures on grain-oriented electrical steel and downstream transformer components from 18 September 2026
keyword: EU provisional safeguard measures grain-oriented electrical steel tariff-rate quota 2026 importer cost
angle: This article lets importers of grain-oriented electrical steel, laminations, cores, and transformers with incorporated cores confirm the scope of new provisional EU safeguard rules and plan their shipment timelines and cost allocations accordingly.

figures.unit: standard maximum duration of a EU safeguard investigation
figures.period: applicable to all ongoing EU safeguard investigations
figures.source: European Commission Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: A safeguard investigation must normally be completed within nine months but, in exceptional circumstances, may be extended to 11 months.

figures.unit: minimum number of EU Member States required to vote in favour for definitive safeguard measures to enter into force

figures.evidence: This means that at least 15 EU Member States representing 65% of the EU’s population must vote in favour of the Commission's proposal.

figures.unit: launch date of the grain-oriented electrical steel safeguard investigation
figures.source: European Commission Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: After analysing input received from interested parties during an investigation launched in March 2026 , the Commission concluded that provisional measures were urgently needed to protect a strategic EU industry that is under threat from high import pressure – fuelled by global overcapacities and the closure of traditional export markets.

figures.unit: effective date of the provisional GOES safeguard measures
figures.source: European Commission Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: Today, the European Commission imposed provisional safeguard measures on imports of grain-oriented electrical steel products, in the form of tariff-rate quotas coupled with price thresholds.
